text:
Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — we're planning to roll the new GPU telemetry JSON logging schema into a prod canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Canary will be 0.5% traffic on prod-gpu-pool-1. Schema adds request_id, model_variant, gpu_id, seq_len, cost_estimate, and a sampled_user_text field (PII redacted). Docs: https://redwood.example/log-schema

Priya Nair: Important — how is sampled_user_text redacted? retention window? we need to be sure legal + security signed off. :eyes:

Alex Chen: sampled_user_text is redacted on ingest: we hash + mask tokens matching our PII regex, then store a 128-bit hash for debug lookup. retention for sampled_user_text is 7 days by default; all other metadata follows existing 90d retention. Security + Legal approved pattern yesterday (see internal thread).

Marco Ruiz: How will this map into Grafana/Prometheus? we must avoid adding high-cardinality labels. gpu_id ok as label for small fleets, but model_variant should NOT be a Prom label unless we aggregate. Suggest we emit metrics with labels: gpu_pool, model_family, slot_type and keep request_id/model_variant in logs only.

Dana Lee: sampling rates? 0.5% is fine for general, but we need per-cluster overrides. Also need an estimate on log volume delta and cost. Last time a schema change doubled our ingest for a week.

Alex Chen: agreed re overrides. Proposed config excerpt: 

```json
{
  "version": "v2",
  "fields": [
    "ts",
    "request_id",
    "model_family",
    "model_variant",
    "gpu_pool",
    "gpu_id",
    "seq_len",
    "lat_ms",
    "cost_usd",
    "sampled_user_text"
  ],
  "pii_redaction": {
    "method": "hash_and_mask",
    "patterns": ["email", "ssn", "credit_card"]
  },
  "sampling": {
    "default_rate": 0.005,
    "overrides": {
      "prod-gpu-pool-1": 0.01,
      "staging-gpu-pool": 0.02
    }
  }
}
```

Alex Chen: rough cost calc from infra: +12% ingest at 0.5% because sampled_user_text is longer but compressed; with current retention that’s ~+$1.2k/month. Overrides increase linearly.

Marco Ruiz: please make sure our ingestion pipeline applies field whitelisting before enrichment so we don't accidentally expand cardinality. Also add a metric 'log_ingest_backpressure' so SRE can alert early.

Lina Gomez: FYI we saw a spike in log_pipeline_errors during the last schema rollout. We should pre-bake an alert runbook: threshold, rollback steps, and paging policy. I'll attach a short runbook to the doc.

Priya Nair: Confirming legal ok with 7-day sampled_user_text retention? can we make that configurable per-customer? some customers require shorter windows.

Alex Chen: yes — retention is per-tenant overrideable via private deployments. For hosted, default 7d but we can shorten for specific customers on request. I'll add a flag in the canary to test override path.

Dana Lee: For dashboards: we need a SLO dashboard that surfaces latency by model_family and cost-per-token by pool. Also a log volume vs. ingest-cost panel. Can we reuse the 'gpu-fleet-cost' grafana folder?

Marco Ruiz: reuse is fine as long as we add a summary panel that removes high-cardinality series. Use topN for model_family and aggregate for gpu_pool.

Alex Chen: plan for rollout: 1) deploy schema parser to canary nodes 02:00 UTC tomorrow (0.5% traffic) 2) monitor ingest errors + log_ingest_backpressure for 30m 3) increase to 2% if stable 4) full rollout over 24h. I'll open the canary now and link monitors.

infra-bot: Canary deployment started at 1765004834 for schema-v2 on prod-gpu-pool-1 :party_parrot:

Lina Gomez: I'll be on-call for the window and will own paging. Dana — can you own the Grafana panels?

Dana Lee: I can. Will add the SLO + cost panels and set alert thresholds for backpressure and error-rate.

Priya Nair: Thanks — please post a short postmortem if anything weird shows up.

Alex Chen: thanks team. Action items: Alex -> update doc with retention overrides; Marco -> ensure no high-cardinality labels; Dana -> dashboards + alerts; Lina -> runbook/paging.
